A. EARTHWORKS: The Contractor shall provide all labour, materials, tools, plant, machinery, transport, and incidentals required to execute comprehensive earthwork operations as detailed below. Thi s includes bulk excavation, banking and embankment construction, and precision backfilling/plinth filling operations. All works shall be performed in strict accordance with the project drawings, design specifications, and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. 1. Earthwork in Excavation by Mechanical / Manual Means over Areas: 1.1 Description of Work Excavation by mechanical means (Hydraulic excavator) or manual means over broad areas exceeding 30 cm in depth, 1.5 m in width, as well as 10 sqm on plan. The scope covers all kinds of soil, including the extraction ('getting out') and neat disposal of the excavated material within a horizontal lead of up to 50 metres and a vertical lift of up to 1.5 metres. 1.2 Technical Specifications & Execution � Method of Excavation: Excavation may be carried out using mechanical plant (hydraulic excavators, backhoes) or by manual labor, depending on site accessibility, safety, and constraints, ensuring no damage to adjacent structures or utilities. � Strata Handling: The execution applies universally to all kinds of soil (including soft, dense, cohesive, non-cohesive, sandy, clayey, or gravelly soils mixed with boulders up to standard size dimensions) without separate classification rates. � Getting Out & Stacking: 'Getting out' shall mean lifting the excavated soil out of the pit, trench, or foundation profile and placing it clearly away from the edges to prevent cave-ins, slippage, or structural instability. � Disposal & Stockpiling: Excavated earth shall be hauled up to a horizontal distance of 50m and a vertical lift of 1.5m. The soil must be neatly deposited, leveled, or stockpiled at designated locations for future backfilling or disposal as approved by the Engineer-in-Charge. � Trimming & Leveling: The bottom and sides of the excavated areas must be accurately dressed, trimmed to slopes, leveled, and rammed to the exact dimensions, profiles, and invert levels shown on the structural/architectural drawings. 1.3 Site Care & Contractor Responsibilities � Pre-Work Levels: Joint initial ground levels must be recorded by the Contractor and the Engineerin- Charge prior to breaking ground. Protection of Services: The Contractor must take all precautions to locate, mark, and protect existing underground utilities (cables, pipes, drains). Any damage shall be repaired immediately at the

Contractor's own cost. � Shoring & Bracing: Where necessary due to loose soil conditions or depth, the Contractor must provide proper timbering, shoring, or strutting to stabilize excavation faces and ensure workforce safety. � Dewatering: The Contractor shall keep the excavated areas free from surface runoff, rain water, or subsoil water by pumping or bailing if required, providing a dry bed for subsequent works. 2. Earthwork in Embankments, Banking, and Formation Construction 2.1 Description of Work Banking excavated earth in layers not exceeding 20 cm in depth, breaking clods, watering, rolling each layer with a ½ tonne roller or wooden/steel rammers, and rolling every 3rd and top-most layer with a power roller of minimum 8 tonnes. Scope includes dressing up in embankments for roads, flood banks, marginal banks, and guide banks, or filling up ground depressions for all kinds of soil, within a horizontal lead up to 50 m and a vertical lift up to 1.5 m. 2.2 Technical Specifications & Execution � Excavation & Materials: Excavate all kinds of soil within the specified lead and lift. The excavated earth must be free from organic matter, large roots, stumps, slush, or any other detrimental material before use in banking. � Layering & Clod Breaking: Deposit the excavated earth in regular, uniform layers not exceeding 20 cm in loose depth. All soil clods, lumps, or hard masses must be thoroughly broken down to a maximum size specified by the Engineer-in-Charge before compaction begins. � Moisture Control (Watering): Add water uniformly to each layer to achieve the Optimum Moisture Content (OMC) required for maximum dry density. The Contractor must ensure uniform moisture distribution across the entire layer. � Initial Compaction: Compact each 20 cm layer thoroughly using a ½ tonne roller or approved wooden/steel hand rammers to eliminate voids. � Heavy Compaction: Roll every 3rd layer and the final top-most layer with a power-driven road roller of a minimum 8 tonnes capacity (or as directed to achieve the specified design density). � Finishing (Dressing): Dress, trim, and grade the final surfaces, slopes, and shoulders of the embankments or filled depressions strictly to the designated lines, grades, cross-sections, and dimensions shown in the drawings. 2.3 Contractor Responsibilities & Equipment � Machinery & Tools: Supply all necessary plant and equipment, including but not limited to excavators, tractors/tippers (if required), water tankers with sprinklers, ½ tonne rollers, hand rammers, and power rollers (minimum 8 tonnes). � Survey & Layout: Establish benchmarks and reference lines. Take initial ground levels jointly with the Engineer-in-Charge prior to starting any excavation or filling.

� Quality Control: Perform routine field density tests (e.g., core cutter or sand replacement method) to ensure the required compaction percentage is achieved before proceeding to subsequent layers. 3. Filling and Backfilling with Available Excavated Earth 3.1 Description of Work Filling available excavated earth (excluding rock) in trenches, plinth, sides of foundations, etc., in layers not exceeding 20 cm in depth. The scope includes consolidating each deposited layer by ramming and watering, with a horizontal lead up to 50 m and a vertical lift up to 1.5 m. 3.2 Material Specifications & Preparation � Source of Material: Only approved, selected earth obtained from site excavations shall be utilized. The backfill material must be completely free from rocks, boulders, hard strata debris, organic matter, roots, large clods, or any highly plastic or expansive clays. � Foundation Clearing: Prior to commencing any filling operations, the target area (trenches, plinths, or foundation pockets) must be completely cleared of all construction debris, shuttering materials, loose masonry, accumulated water, and slush. 3.3 Execution & Consolidation Steps � Layered Placement: The earth shall be deposited and spread in regular, horizontal, and uniform layers not exceeding 20 cm in loose depth. � Moisture Conditioning: Each layer shall be lightly sprinkled with water uniformly. The moisture content must be carefully controlled and distributed to ensure optimal compaction without turning the soil into mud or slush. � Consolidation (Ramming): Each watered layer must be thoroughly consolidated using approved mechanical compactors, plate vibrators, or heavy hand rammers. Ramming must continue until the layer is densely packed, shows no signs of yielding, and achieves a solid, unyielding matrix before the subsequent layer is laid. � Consecutive Work: Successive layers of 20 cm shall be built up in this exact manner until the design finished level or sub-grade line is reached. B. Demolition, Plain Concrete, and Composite R.C.C. Decking: The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, tools, plant, scaffolding, safety apparatus, and machinery required to execute three interrelated civil phases strictly as detailed in this document and under the guidance of the Engineer-in-Charge: 1. Structural Demolition of R.C.C. Work � Execution Methodology: Demolition shall be performed carefully via manual labor (using jackhammers, chisels, sledges) or mechanical means (hydraulic rock breakers, concrete cutters) as site conditions dictate. The Contractor must ensure zero structural distress, vibration cracking, or damage to adjacent structures, active utility networks, or surrounding property. � Rebar Extraction & Stacking: Embedded steel reinforcement bars must be carefully detached and extricated from the collapsing concrete matrix. Extracted rebar shall be cleaned of adhering concrete

chunks, straightened, sorted by nominal diameter, and neatly stacked at designated salvage yards within a horizontal lead of 100 meters. � Debris Extraction & Disposal: All unserviceable concrete rubble, debris, and dust must be collected immediately, damped down to control air pollution, and hauled for legal disposal at approved site dumping zones within a horizontal lead of 100 meters, as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. 2. Providing & Laying Plain Cement Concrete (P.C.C. 1:3:6) � Material Mix Specification: The volumetric mix ratio shall be strictly 1:3:6—comprising 1 part Portland Cement, 3 parts clean coarse sand, and 6 parts graded stone aggregate of 20 mm nominal size. All constituent materials must comply with local engineering validation codes. � Mixing & Placement: Batching must be precise. Concrete shall be mechanically mixed in a drum mixer to achieve a uniform, homogenous consistency. P.C.C. shall be laid in true positions, levels, and designated layer thicknesses over a cleaned, well-compacted subgrade bed. � Compaction & Curing: The laid concrete must be thoroughly consolidated using mechanical plate compactors or screed vibrators to eradicate internal air pockets and voids. The finished surfaces must be kept continuously wet for a minimum curing duration of 7 days. 3. Reinforced Cement Concrete with Steel Decking Sheet (R.C.C. 1:1.5:3) � Material Mix Specification: The volumetric mix ratio shall be strictly 1:1.5:3—comprising 1 part Portland cement, 1.5 parts clean coarse sand, and 3 parts graded stone aggregate of 20 mm nominal size, engineered to yield structural grade durability. � Profile Steel Decking Integration: During the construction of structural floor slabs, the Contractor must supply and install structural galvanized profile steel decking sheets to serve as a permanent composite diaphragm formwork. The sheets must be securely fastened to the underlying structural steel or concrete support framework via shear studs or approved fastening pins before concrete placement. � Placement & Heights: The structural concrete mix shall be poured directly over the installed deck profile and reinforcing mesh. Concrete drop heights must not exceed 1.5 meters to prevent aggregate segregation. The work applies universally to all structural floor levels and vertical heights. � Mixing & Placement: Batching must be precise. Concrete shall be mechanically mixed in a drum mixer to achieve a uniform, homogenous consistency. C.C. shall be laid in true positions, levels, and designated layer thicknesses over a cleaned, well-compacted bed. � Compaction & Curing: The laid concrete must be thoroughly consolidated using mechanical plate compactors or screed vibrators to eradicate internal air pockets and voids. The finished surfaces must be kept continuously wet for a minimum curing duration of 7 days. C. Sand Filling in Plinth Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Source & Quality: Sand shall be clean, sharp, angular, and free from clay, loam, organic impurities,

or salts. � Execution: Spread uniformly in regular layers not exceeding 15 cm in depth. � Consolidation: Each layer must be thoroughly watered, rammed mechanically or manually, and consolidated until a firm sub grade matrix is established. � Dressing: The final layer must be meticulously dressed to true levels, matching design sub-base requirements. D. Steel Reinforcement for R.C.C. Work Technical Scope & Execution Clauses:(Contractor should submit bar bending schedule) � Material Grade: Strictly Thermo-Mechanically Treated (TMT) steel bars of grade Fe-500D or higher conforming to standard regulatory codes. � Processing & Delivery: Rebars must arrive at the site pre-cut and bent from an approved factory/workshop according to verified Bar Bending Schedules (BBS). � Placement: Securely position rebars inside formwork using concrete spacer blocks, chairs, and approved mechanical supports. � Binding: Tie all intersections completely using 16 SWG black annealed binding wire. E. Centering and Shuttering (Below Plinth Level) Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Material Quality: Rigid timber, marine-grade plywood, or steel plates designed to prevent mortar leakage and buckling. � Stability & Propping: Struts and props must be adequately anchored and braced to withstand concrete structural loads. � Removal (Stripping): Retain formwork until concrete achieves self-supporting strength; remove safely under supervision. � Application Scope: Pertains to substructure components including footings, pile caps, foundation beams, and columns below plinth. F. Centering and Shuttering (Above Plinth Level) Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Surface Finish: Formwork must give a smooth, clean concrete texture free from honeycomb defects or physical waviness. � Camber: Provide specified upward camber in structural beams and roof slab soffits to counteract elastic deflection. � Safety & Liftoff: Formwork at higher elevations must integrate safety scaffolding, working platforms, and perimeter protection nets. � Application Scope: Covers all superstructure components including columns, beams, lintels, roof slabs, and projections. G. Dry Stone Pitching

Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Stone Selection: Sound, durable, hard quarry stones free from cracks and weathering defects, with a minimum thickness of 22.5 cm. � Bed Preparation: The underlying earthen slope or formation bed must be cleared, dressed to a true profile, and heavily rammed. � Interlocking Layout: Stones shall be placed closely by hand, breaking joints, with larger stones placed at the toe. Interstices must be tightly keyed using smaller stone spalls. H. Providing and Grouting Pockets Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Material Specification: Pre-bagged, non-shrink, high-strength, free-flowing cementitious grout from an approved manufacturing brand. � Preparation: Clean foundation bolt pockets of all loose debris, dust, and oil. Pre-soak concrete with water to a saturated surface-dry (SSD) state. � Grouting Operation: Mix mechanically and place/pump continuously to eliminate air voids. Use heavy-duty free-flowing grout pumps where deep pockets exist. � Curing & Metrics: Keep grouted pockets continuously damp for a minimum of 7 days. Billing is determined strictly by the actual dry weight (kg/tonne) of approved grout consumed. I. Neat Cement Punning Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Application Technique: Apply a smooth, uniform coat of neat cement slurry over a fresh, damp cement plaster base. � Finishing: Trowel continuously with steel floats to create a slick, glossy, water-resistant surface texture completely free from trowel marks. � Curing: Protect from rapid drying and cure continuously for a minimum of 7 days. J. Structural Steel Work Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Fabrication Constraints: Precision cutting, drilling, and shaping of structural profiles. Connections must be executed via standard welding, riveting, or high-strength bolting. � Erection & Safety: Hoisting, aligning, and securely anchoring trusses, purlins, columns, and frames using crane machinery and guy-wires. � Corrosion Protection: Clean steel surfaces via wire brushing/sandblasting. Apply one uniform coat of approved anti-corrosive primer followed by two complete finishing coats of high-gloss synthetic enamel paint. K. Glazed Stoneware Pipes Installation Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Pipe Class: Premium 150 mm nominal diameter glazed stoneware pipes of Class SP1 conforming to

strict sanitary design standards. � Trench Bedding: Lay pipes true to line and grade on a prepared uniform trench floor, socket ends facing upstream. � Jointing Matrix: Pack joints tightly using gaskin tarred yarn followed by a stiff cement mortar mix of 1:1 proportion (1 cement: 1 fine sand), finished with a neat 45-degree mortar fillet. � Testing Protocol: Conduct mandatory hydraulic smoke or water-head testing to guarantee absolute watertight performance before backfilling. L. Construction of Masonry Valve Chamber Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Excavation & Sub-Base: Excavate to required structural depths. Lay a firm foundation mat of 1:5:10 PCC (1 cement: 5 fine sand: 10 graded 40 mm stone aggregate). � Superstructure Masonry: Build clear internal dimensions of 120x120x100 cm utilizing common burnt clay F.P.S. bricks (class designation 7.5) embedded in a 1:4 cement mortar mix. � Internal Plaster & Punning: Apply a 12 mm thick internal plaster coat using 1:3 cement mortar, topped with a smooth floating coat of neat cement. � Top Slab & Access: Cast a structural R.C.C. roof cover slab using a 1:2:4 mix (20 mm aggregate) embedded with a heavy-duty Cast Iron (C.I.) surface box featuring a chained secure lid. � Rate Inclusions: The item rate is completely comprehensive for excavation, masonry, concrete work, reinforcement, plastering, punning, and fixing the iron hardware components. M. Demolishing Brick Work Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Execution Strategy: Carefully demolish brick masonry walls or elements laid in cement mortar without shocking adjacent structural components. � Salvage Control: Extract, clean, and neatly stack reusable, undamaged whole bricks within a horizontal lead of 50 meters. � Waste Disposal: Collect unserviceable structural rubble, transport, and dump at authorized disposal piles within a 50m lead boundary. N. Fly Ash Brick Masonry Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Material Guidelines: Eco-friendly non-modular fly ash building bricks conforming strictly to standard building codes, possessing an average compressive strength class designation of 10. � Workmanship: Lay bricks uniformly in standard running bond, ensuring fully packed vertical and horizontal mortar joints. � Elevational Bounds: The item rate applies to all superstructure levels from plinth up to Floor Level V without separate height modification charges. O. Textured Exterior Wall Finish

Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Surface Maturation: Plastered walls must be fully cured, dry, clean, and structurally sound prior to product coat application. � Primer Sub-Base: Apply one comprehensive coat of specialized exterior primer at a strict application matrix of 2.20 kg per 10 square metres. � Textured Coating: Apply two or more coats of approved premium textured exterior paint of designated color shade at a coverage rate of 3.28 litres per 10 square metres. P. Acrylic Emulsion Exterior Painting Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Material Standard: Premium 100% acrylic emulsion paint infused with silicon additives, showing VOC limits under 50 gm/liter, UV-stabilized, anti-fungal, and dirt-resistant attributes. � Primer Integration: Apply one foundation layer of high-adhesion exterior wall primer at a strict index of 0.90 liters per 10 square meters. � Finishing Coats: Apply two or more finishing coats of factory depot-tinted paint at a spread benchmark of 1.43 liters per 10 square meters. Q. 15 mm Cement Plastering Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Mix Balance: Volumetric mix ratio shall be strictly 1:6—comprising 1 part Portland Cement to 6 parts clean fine sand. � Execution Depth: Apply in a single uniform layer maintaining a nominal finished depth profile of 15 mm, troweled to plumb lines and sharp corners. � Height Flexibility: Rate applies universally across all construction vertical scaffolding heights and lead spaces. R. Random Rubble Stone Masonry Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Stone Integrity: Utilize selected hard, durable quarry stones properly dressed at faces and corners. � Mortar Matrix: Bind masonry structural units securely using a 1:6 cement mortar mix (1 cement : 6 clean coarse sand). � Leveling Layers: Bring up walls in courses and level off at designated heights utilizing a solid 1:6:12 PCC mix (20 mm aggregate). � Comprehensive Constraints: Unit rate accounts for all rock components, specialized tools, heavy scaffolding, labor, and leveling processes below plinth. S. Collapsible Steel Shutters Technical Scope & Execution Clauses: � Structural Frame: Fabricated using 20x10x2 mm vertical steel channels braced with heavy 20x5 mm flat iron diagonal cross-sections.

� Guide Tracks: Provide robust top and bottom guide rails rolled from durable 40x40x6 mm T-iron sections. � Hardware Integration: Equip assemblies with 40 mm diameter heavy-duty steel ball-bearing pulleys, handles, security locking ears, and slide stoppers. � Coating: Clean all steel components thoroughly and apply one uniform protective layer of approved anti-corrosive structural steel primer. A. EARTHWORKS: The Contractor shall provide all labour, materials, tools, plant, machinery, transport, and incidentals required to execute comprehensive earthwork operations as detailed below. Thi s includes bulk excavation, banking and embankment construction, and precision backfilling/plinth filling operations. All works shall be performed in strict accordance with the project drawings, design specifications, and directions of the Engineer-in-Charge. 1. Earthwork in Excavation by Mechanical / Manual Means over Areas: 1.1 Description of Work Excavation by mechanical means (Hydraulic excavator) or manual means over broad areas exceeding 30 cm in depth, 1.5 m in width, as well as 10 sqm on plan. The scope covers all kinds of soil, including the extraction ('getting out') and neat disposal of the excavated material within a horizontal lead of up to 50 metres and a vertical lift of up to 1.5 metres. 1.2 Technical Specifications & Execution � Method of Excavation: Excavation may be carried out using mechanical plant (hydraulic excavators, backhoes) or by manual labor, depending on site accessibility, safety, and constraints, ensuring no damage to adjacent structures or utilities. � Strata Handling: The execution applies universally to all kinds of soil (including soft, dense, cohesive, non-cohesive, sandy, clayey, or gravelly soils mixed with boulders up to standard size dimensions) without separate classification rates. � Getting Out & Stacking: 'Getting out' shall mean lifting the excavated soil out of the pit, trench, or foundation profile and placing it clearly away from the edges to prevent cave-ins, slippage, or structural instability. � Disposal & Stockpiling: Excavated earth shall be hauled up to a horizontal distance of 50m and a vertical lift of 1.5m. The soil must be neatly deposited, leveled, or stockpiled at designated locations for future backfilling or disposal as approved by the Engineer-in-Charge. � Trimming & Leveling: The bottom and sides of the excavated areas must be accurately dressed, trimmed to slopes, leveled, and rammed to the exact dimensions, profiles, and invert levels shown on the structural/architectural drawings. 1.3 Site Care & Contractor Responsibilities � Pre-Work Levels: Joint initial ground levels must be recorded by the Contractor and the Engineerin- Charge prior to breaking ground. Protection of Services: The Contractor must take all precautions to locate, mark, and protect existing underground utilities (cables, pipes, drains). Any damage shall be repaired immediately at the

Contractor's own cost. � Shoring & Bracing: Where necessary due to loose soil conditions or depth, the Contractor must provide proper timbering, shoring, or strutting to stabilize excavation faces and ensure workforce safety. � Dewatering: The Contractor shall keep the excavated areas free from surface runoff, rain water, or subsoil water by pumping or bailing if required, providing a dry bed for subsequent works. 2. Earthwork in Embankments, Banking, and Formation Construction 2.1 Description of Work Banking excavated earth in layers not exceeding 20 cm in depth, breaking clods, watering, rolling each layer with a ½ tonne roller or wooden/steel rammers, and rolling every 3rd and top-most layer with a power roller of minimum 8 tonnes. Scope includes dressing up in embankments for roads, flood banks, marginal banks, and guide banks, or filling up ground depressions for all kinds of soil, within a horizontal lead up to 50 m and a vertical lift up to 1.5 m. 2.2 Technical Specifications & Execution � Excavation & Materials: Excavate all kinds of soil within the specified lead and lift. The excavated earth must be free from organic matter, large roots, stumps, slush, or any other detrimental material before use in banking. � Layering & Clod Breaking: Deposit the excavated earth in regular, uniform layers not exceeding 20 cm in loose depth. All soil clods, lumps, or hard masses must be thoroughly broken down to a maximum size specified by the Engineer-in-Charge before compaction begins. � Moisture Control (Watering): Add water uniformly to each layer to achieve the Optimum Moisture Content (OMC) required for maximum dry density. The Contractor must ensure uniform moisture distribution across the entire layer. � Initial Compaction: Compact each 20 cm layer thoroughly using a ½ tonne roller or approved wooden/steel hand rammers to eliminate voids. � Heavy Compaction: Roll every 3rd layer and the final top-most layer with a power-driven road roller of a minimum 8 tonnes capacity (or as directed to achieve the specified design density). � Finishing (Dressing): Dress, trim, and grade the final surfaces, slopes, and shoulders of the embankments or filled depressions strictly to the designated lines, grades, cross-sections, and dimensions shown in the drawings. 2.3 Contractor Responsibilities & Equipment � Machinery & Tools: Supply all necessary plant and equipment, including but not limited to excavators, tractors/tippers (if required), water tankers with sprinklers, ½ tonne rollers, hand rammers, and power rollers (minimum 8 tonnes). � Survey & Layout: Establish benchmarks and reference lines. Take initial ground levels jointly with the Engineer-in-Charge prior to starting any excavation or filling.

� Quality Control: Perform routine field density tests (e.g., core cutter or sand replacement method) to ensure the required compaction percentage is achieved before proceeding to subsequent layers. 3. Filling and Backfilling with Available Excavated Earth 3.1 Description of Work Filling available excavated earth (excluding rock) in trenches, plinth, sides of foundations, etc., in layers not exceeding 20 cm in depth. The scope includes consolidating each deposited layer by ramming and watering, with a horizontal lead up to 50 m and a vertical lift up to 1.5 m. 3.2 Material Specifications & Preparation � Source of Material: Only approved, selected earth obtained from site excavations shall be utilized. The backfill material must be completely free from rocks, boulders, hard strata debris, organic matter, roots, large clods, or any highly plastic or expansive clays. � Foundation Clearing: Prior to commencing any filling operations, the target area (trenches, plinths, or foundation pockets) must be completely cleared of all construction debris, shuttering materials, loose masonry, accumulated water, and slush. 3.3 Execution & Consolidation Steps � Layered Placement: The earth shall be deposited and spread in regular, horizontal, and uniform layers not exceeding 20 cm in loose depth. � Moisture Conditioning: Each layer shall be lightly sprinkled with water uniformly. The moisture content must be carefully controlled and distributed to ensure optimal compaction without turning the soil into mud or slush. � Consolidation (Ramming): Each watered layer must be thoroughly consolidated using approved mechanical compactors, plate vibrators, or heavy hand rammers. Ramming must continue until the layer is densely packed, shows no signs of yielding, and achieves a solid, unyielding matrix before the subsequent layer is laid. � Consecutive Work: Successive layers of 20 cm shall be built up in this exact manner until the design finished level or sub-grade line is reached. chunks, straightened, sorted by nominal diameter, and neatly stacked at designated salvage yards within a horizontal lead of 100 meters. � Debris Extraction & Disposal: All unserviceable concrete rubble, debris, and dust must be collected immediately, damped down to control air pollution, and hauled for legal disposal at approved site dumping zones within a horizontal lead of 100 meters, as directed by the Engineer-in-Charge. 2. Providing & Laying Plain Cement Concrete (P.C.C. 1:3:6) � Material Mix Specification: The volumetric mix ratio shall be strictly 1:3:6—comprising 1 part Portland Cement, 3 parts clean coarse sand, and 6 parts graded stone aggregate of 20 mm nominal size. All constituent materials must comply with local engineering validation codes. � Mixing & Placement: Batching must be precise.
